title: Bellarmine's OT silence example flips to NT instances — Mary's perpetual virginity first
source_text: XX. Et istud quidem profert Bellarminus, cujus praecipue vestigia sequimur, tanquam exemplum rei necessariae sub Veteri Testamento, de qua tamen in Scriptura sacra nihil reperitur. Quod autem hodie sub Novo Testamento multa ad fidem pertineant de quibus per Scripturam doceri non possumus, pluribus instantiis probare annititur. Et primum quidem, inquit, credendum est Beatam Mariam semper fuisse virginem contra errorem Helvidii, ut semper tota Ecclesia credidit. Et tamen nullum de hac re est in Scriptura testimonium.
pass_a_gloss: And indeed Bellarmine, whose footsteps we chiefly follow, brings this forward as an example of a necessary matter under the Old Testament of which yet nothing is found in sacred Scripture. But that today under the New Testament many things belong to the faith about which we cannot be taught through Scripture, he strives to prove by several instances. And first indeed, he says, it must be believed that the Blessed Mary was always a virgin against the error of Helvidius, as the whole Church has always believed. And yet there is no testimony on this matter in Scripture.
pass_b_english: Bellarmine offers that Old-Testament silence as a specimen of something necessary yet unwritten.
He then piles New-Testament instances of faith-matters he says Scripture cannot teach.
First: Mary always a virgin against Helvidius — Church-wide belief, he says, with no Scriptural witness.
